backgrounds: Single continuous set for the entire episode: a stylized stop-motion apartment kitchen at night, shot from one fixed camera angle (a slight low/waist-height angle on the two characters standing center-frame). The kitchen has upper and lower taupe/beige cabinetry, tan tile backsplash, a checkerboard (cream and grey) tile floor, a window over the sink looking out onto a dark city skyline with lit windows (establishes night-time, apartment/high-rise setting), and an oven/stove-dishwasher-fridge run of appliances on the right side. A wooden dining table with an upholstered chair is visible at the far left edge of frame. The only other 'location' is a plain black title-card background used for the intro/outro text (episode number, series title, 'Adult Love' episode title, 'created by Nin.' credit, and 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' badge) — this is graphic overlay, not a physical set.

A takeout food container/plate with what looks like a burger and fries
Dish rack with plates and a blue sponge/scrubber

Wedding/engagement ring visible on the man's hand as the couple holds hands
lighting_notes: Warm, soft interior kitchen lighting (practical-looking, slightly amber) contrasts with the cool deep-blue night visible through the window, giving clear separation between the intimate lit interior and the cold exterior. Lighting is even and flattering on the character faces with gentle shadow falloff typical of stop-motion/miniature set lighting (soft key light, mild rim light from the window side). No dramatic lighting changes occur during the scene — it stays consistent throughout, reinforcing the calm, late-night domestic mood.
color_palette: deep navy blue (night sky through window)
warm skin-tone peach/tan (character faces and hands)
black and white (man's suit, shirt, tie)
mustard yellow accent (title card text and 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' badge)
visual_complexity_notes: The set is a single, moderately detailed but realistic-feeling miniature kitchen — more 'lived-in dense' than minimal, with lots of small background clutter (takeout boxes, fruit bowl, dish rack, soap bottle, slippers) that reads as deliberate scene-setting for a believable apartment rather than randomly busy. Despite the detailed environment, the camera holds a single static composition on the two characters throughout almost the entire runtime, so visual complexity in the background does not compete with focus on the characters' faces and dialogue — the dense, homey clutter reinforces an 'ordinary domestic evening' tone while the unchanging frame keeps attention on the couple's expressions and conversation.
